title: Resolve parser stage and protocol role before broadening leniency
applies_when: An incremental protocol parser returns NEED_DATA, two framing helpers accept different delimiters, or an audit infers receiver obligations from a sender prohibition or a file-level comment.
lesson: Trace the actual public caller, grammar stage and end-of-input path before proposing a permissiveness fix. In h11, header extraction accepts bare LF while the chunk-size reader uses a CRLF-only helper; these are different grammar stages, not automatically inconsistent contracts. A pending result before EOF is not proof of a hang: feed explicit EOF through Connection and inspect its error, with a valid-message control. Distinguish sender, recipient and intermediary obligations in the applicable protocol revision. The existing h11 #90 discussion explains why a sender's CL+TE prohibition alone does not prove that a recipient must reject the message. Parsing precedence, forwarding normalization and connection reuse are separate questions; test the particular obligation rather than declaring the whole behavior correct or defective.
avoid_when: A comment or older issue does not override a newer applicable standard. RFC9112 allows rejection or TE-only processing but separately requires closing after responding to a request containing both CL and TE; correct body framing alone cannot settle that obligation. No deployment vulnerability, exploitability, novelty or complete conformance follows from a sans-I/O characterization. Do not expand chunk-body leniency merely to match header parsing: h11's published advisory documents a prior malformed-footer parser differential. Ordinary pytest success is not coverage, all-version CI or a measured improvement in Scout discovery, conversion or misses.

evidence.note: Pinned helpers implement distinct CRLF line extraction and permissive header-block extraction. File-level commentary alone is not a per-caller contract.

ChunkedReader uses maybe_extract_next_line for the chunk header, verifies chunk-footer CRLF and raises RemoteProtocolError on an incomplete chunked read at EOF. This establishes mechanisms, not all network-service behavior.

The maintainer's existing RFC7230 discussion distinguishes sender restrictions from recipient framing and unresolved interoperability choices. This is prior public discussion, not a novel report or approval of a new patch.

The current standard separates recipient handling of CL+TE from the subsequent close requirement. Check the applicable role and lifecycle obligation independently; the older issue does not establish present-day conformance.

Published historical advisory describes malformed chunk-footer parsing and conditions involving a differently parsing proxy. It cautions against indiscriminate leniency; it is not evidence of a new vulnerability in current source.
